## Preprocessing

Use the generated_data and split manifest to get the training, validation, and test sets.

```{r}
source("R/preprocessing.R")

cleaned <- read.csv("Generated_Data/cleaned_data.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))
manifest <- read.csv("Generated_Data/split_manifest.csv")
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(cleaned$CustomerID),
  !anyDuplicated(manifest$CustomerID),
  setequal(cleaned$CustomerID, manifest$CustomerID)
)
data <- cleaned[match(manifest$CustomerID, cleaned$CustomerID),]
data$split <- manifest$split
data$cv_fold <- manifest$cv_fold
data <- add_cell2cell_features(data)

# Separate training and test data
training <- subset(data, split == "train")
test <- subset(data, split == "test")

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(training$cv_fold),
  setequal(unique(training$cv_fold), 1:3),
  all(is.na(test$cv_fold))
)

table(training$cv_fold)
table(training$Churn)

# dimensions
dim(training)
dim(test)
```

There are three recommended predictor sets for the logistic regression model. I will train a model using each predictor set at each outreach capacity (0.1, 0.2, 0.3).

The predictor set labelled `focused_both` contains the following variables. Among all predictor sets, MonthsInService is transformed using a natural cubic spline (df = 3). 

`focused_both` contains the interaction term between `MonthsInSerive` and `CurrentEquipmentDays`.

`focused_missing` contains the same features but without this interaction term.

`broader_without_price` is the same set of features as before but with additional features such as handset information, usage costs and roaming, customer history, and calling activity.

```{r}
# Retrieve logistic regression predictor groups
handoff_predictors <- cell2cell_handoff_predictors()
logistic_terms <- handoff_predictors$logistic

logistic_terms$focused_both
logistic_terms$focused_missing
logistic_terms$broader_without_price
```


```{r}
# Three candidate models
model_terms <- list(
  focused_both = logistic_terms$focused_both,
  focused_missing = logistic_terms$focused_missing,
  broader_without_price = logistic_terms$broader_without_price
)

# Convert predictor lists into formulas
model_formulas <- lapply(
  model_terms,
  function(terms) {
    reformulate(terms, response = "churn_flag")
  }
)
# View the three formulas
# model_formulas
```



```{r}
# All unique predictors used across the three models
inputs <- unique(unlist(
  lapply(unlist(model_terms, use.names = FALSE), function(term) {
    all.vars(parse(text = term))
  }),
  use.names = FALSE
))
```


The model is evaluated on three outreach capacities, which looks for customers in the top 10%, 20%, and 30% highest risk of churning.

```{r}
capacities <- c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30)

evaluate_logistic <- function(actual,probability,customer_id,model_name,fold_id) {

  outcome <- as.numeric(as.character(actual))
  
  positives <- sum(outcome == 1) # churned
  negatives <- sum(outcome == 0) # did not churn

  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(outcome),
    positives > 0,
    negatives > 0
  )
  # auc formula
  auc <- (
    sum(rank(probability)[outcome == 1]) -
      positives * (positives + 1) / 2
  ) / (positives * negatives)
  # customer ranking
  ranked <- order(-probability, customer_id)

  # Evaluate different outreach capacities
  precision <- vapply(capacities, function(capacity) {
    n_contact <- floor(capacity * length(ranked))
    contacted <- head(ranked, n_contact)
    mean(outcome[contacted] == 1)
  }, numeric(1))

  # Lift relative to overall churn rate
  lift <- precision / mean(outcome == 1)

  data.frame(
    Model = model_name,
    Fold = fold_id,
    Capacity = capacities,
    AUC = auc,
    Precision = precision,
    Lift = lift
  )
}
```


### Three-fold Validation Step

```{r}
fold_results <- list()
fold_models <- list()

for (fold_id in 1:3) {
  cat("Validation fold:", fold_id, "\n")

  # Split analysis and assessment data
  analysis <- training[training$cv_fold != fold_id, ] # training fold
  assessment <- training[training$cv_fold == fold_id, ] # validation fold

  # Preprocess using analysis data only
  processed <- prepare_cell2cell_fold(
    analysis,
    assessment,
    inputs
  )
  analysis <- processed$analysis
  assessment <- processed$assessment

  # Fit and evaluate all three models
  fold_results[[fold_id]] <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(model_terms), function(candidate) {

      formula <- model_formulas[[candidate]]

      # Fit logistic regression
      fit <- glm(
        formula,
        family = binomial(),
        data = analysis,
        na.action = na.fail
      )
      stopifnot(
        fit$converged,
        nobs(fit) == nrow(analysis)
      )

      # Predict churn probabilities
      probability <- predict(
        fit,
        newdata = assessment,
        type = "response"
      )
      stopifnot(
        length(probability) == nrow(assessment),
        all(is.finite(probability))
      )

      # Evaluate model
      results <- evaluate_logistic(
        actual = assessment$churn_flag,
        probability = probability,
        customer_id = assessment$CustomerID,
        model_name = candidate,
        fold_id = fold_id
      )

      # Save fitted model
      fold_models[[paste(candidate, fold_id, sep = "_")]] <<- fit

      results
    })
  )
}

# Combine results from all folds
fold_scores <- do.call(rbind, fold_results)
row.names(fold_scores) <- NULL
fold_scores
```


```{r}
cv_summary <- aggregate(
  cbind(AUC, Precision, Lift) ~ Model + Capacity,
  data = fold_scores,
  FUN = mean
)

# Calculate standard deviation across folds
cv_sd <- aggregate(
  cbind(AUC, Precision, Lift) ~ Model + Capacity,
  data = fold_scores,
  FUN = sd
)

names(cv_sd)[names(cv_sd) == "AUC"] <- "AUC_SD"
names(cv_sd)[names(cv_sd) == "Precision"] <- "Precision_SD"
names(cv_sd)[names(cv_sd) == "Lift"] <- "Lift_SD"

# Combine mean and standard deviation
cv_summary <- merge(
  cv_summary,
  cv_sd,
  by = c("Model", "Capacity")
)

cv_summary <- cv_summary[
  order(
    -cv_summary$Precision,
    -cv_summary$AUC,
    -cv_summary$Lift
  ),
]

print(cv_summary, row.names = FALSE)
```
Based on the summary, focused_both model provides the highest precision and AUC at 10% outreach capacity. Let us explore this group more by training it on the full training data and validating it on the test data.

### Final Logistic Regression Model

```{r}
# Preprocess full training data and reserved test data
final_processed <- prepare_cell2cell_fold(
  training,
  test,
  inputs
)

final_training <- final_processed$analysis
final_test <- final_processed$assessment

# Select focused_both
selected_model <- "focused_both"

# Fit logistic regression
final_logit <- glm(
  model_formulas[[selected_model]],
  family = binomial(),
  data = final_training,
  na.action = na.fail
)

# Inspect model summary
# summary(final_logit) 
```


```{r}
test_results <- evaluate_logistic(
  actual = final_test$churn_flag,
  probability = predict(
    final_logit,
    newdata = final_test,
    type = "response"
  ),
  customer_id = final_test$CustomerID,
  model_name = "focused_both",
  fold_id = "Test"
)

print(test_results, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Confusion Matrix

```{r}
# Get predicted probabilities
test_probability <- predict(
  final_logit,
  newdata = final_test,
  type = "response"
)

# Function to calculate confusion matrix at an outreach capacity
get_churn_matrix <- function(actual, probability, capacity) {

  # Determine probability cutoff for the selected capacity
  cutoff <- quantile(
    probability,
    probs = 1 - capacity,
    type = 1
  )

  # Rank customers by predicted probability
  predicted <- ifelse(probability >= cutoff, 1, 0)

  # Create confusion matrix
  table(
    Actual = factor(actual, levels = c(0, 1)),
    Predicted = factor(predicted, levels = c(0, 1))
  )
}

# Calculate matrices
matrix_10 <- get_churn_matrix(
  final_test$churn_flag,
  test_probability,
  0.10
)

matrix_20 <- get_churn_matrix(
  final_test$churn_flag,
  test_probability,
  0.20
)

matrix_30 <- get_churn_matrix(
  final_test$churn_flag,
  test_probability,
  0.30
)

# Display confusion matrices
cat("Top 10% outreach capacity\n")
matrix_10 # confusion matrix for 10% outreach capacity

cat("Top 20% outreach capacity\n")
matrix_20 # confusion matrix for 20% outreach capacity

cat("Top 30% outreach capacity\n")
matrix_30 # confusion matrix for 30% outreach capacity
```

# Estimated Net Revenue 

The following assumptions are made:

The overall training churn rate is 28.2%. The model will estimate the revenue based on four churn rates (0.15, 0.25, 0.30, 0.40).

Retention success rate will range from (0.15, 0.25, 0.35, 0.45)

Contact cost will range from (2, 3, 4, 5)

Offer cost is the additional cost of the retention incentive given to a customer to encourage them to stay. It can be credit given to the customer, discounts, or additional service. For example, if the offer is 10 dollars off from current monthly plan cost for 3 months, then offer cost would be 30 dollars.


```{r}
# Fixed outreach capacity
outreach_capacity <- 0.10

# Business assumptions to test
churn_rates <- c(0.15, 0.25, 0.30, 0.40)
retention_success_rates <- c(0.15, 0.25, 0.35, 0.45)
contact_costs <- c(2, 3, 4, 5)

# Retention offer cost
offer_costs <- c(0, 20, 30, 50)

# Revenue projection period. This assumes that the customer will stay for the next 12 months after accepting an offer
projection_months <- 12 
```

```{r}
# Predict churn probabilities on the test set
test_probability <- predict(
  final_logit,
  newdata = final_test,
  type = "response"
)

# Observed churn rate in the training dataset
sample_churn_rate <- mean(
  as.numeric(as.character(training$churn_flag))
)

sample_churn_rate
```

Adjusts the model's predicted churn probabilities to reflect an assumed real-world churn rate.

```{r}
adjust_probabilities <- function(probability, sample_rate, target_rate) {

  sample_odds <- probability / (1 - probability)

  adjusted_odds <- sample_odds *
    (target_rate / (1 - target_rate)) /
    (sample_rate / (1 - sample_rate))

  adjusted_probability <- adjusted_odds / (1 + adjusted_odds)

  adjusted_probability
}
```


Calculate Net Revenue for each combination of the assumptions.

```{r}
# Create all combinations of assumptions
scenarios <- expand.grid(
  Churn_Rate = churn_rates,
  Retention_Success_Rate = retention_success_rates,
  Contact_Cost = contact_costs,
  Offer_Cost = offer_costs
)

# Customer monthly revenue
monthly_revenue <- as.numeric(final_test$MonthlyRevenue)

# Number of customers to contact
n_contact <- floor(nrow(final_test) * outreach_capacity)

# Calculate revenue for each scenario
revenue_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(i) {

    scenario <- scenarios[i, ]

    # Adjust probabilities to the assumed real-world churn rate
    adjusted_probability <- adjust_probabilities(
      probability = test_probability,
      sample_rate = sample_churn_rate,
      target_rate = scenario$Churn_Rate
    )

    # Calculate expected monthly revenue at risk
    value_at_risk <- adjusted_probability * monthly_revenue

    # Rank customers by revenue at risk
    ranked_customers <- order(
      -value_at_risk,
      final_test$CustomerID
    )

    # Select customers within outreach capacity
    contacted <- head(ranked_customers, n_contact)

    # Expected number of at-risk customers contacted
    expected_at_risk <- sum(
      adjusted_probability[contacted]
    )

    # Expected number of customers retained
    expected_retained <- expected_at_risk *
      scenario$Retention_Success_Rate

    # Expected 12-month revenue saved
    revenue_saved <- sum(
      adjusted_probability[contacted] *
        scenario$Retention_Success_Rate *
        monthly_revenue[contacted] *
        projection_months
    )

    # Total campaign cost
    campaign_cost <- n_contact * (
      scenario$Contact_Cost + scenario$Offer_Cost
    )

    # Net revenue
    net_revenue <- revenue_saved - campaign_cost

    data.frame(
      Churn_Rate = scenario$Churn_Rate,
      Retention_Success_Rate = scenario$Retention_Success_Rate,
      Contact_Cost = scenario$Contact_Cost,
      Offer_Cost = scenario$Offer_Cost,
      Customers_Contacted = n_contact,
      Expected_At_Risk = expected_at_risk,
      Expected_Retained = expected_retained,
      Revenue_Saved = revenue_saved,
      Campaign_Cost = campaign_cost,
      Net_Revenue = net_revenue
    )
  })
)
row.names(revenue_results) <- NULL
```

In the most obvious sense, Net Revenue is highest when Churn Rate and Retention Rate is high. There are more customers who can potentially be 'saved' by the 'offer,' The higher retention rate means that more of these customers accepted the offer. However, this is the most optimistic scenario. 

```{r}
revenue_results |>
  arrange(desc(Net_Revenue)) |>
  head(10)

# saves the scenario dataframe as a csv
# write.csv(revenue_results, file = "revenue_scenarios/logistic_revenue_estimates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

This may not be the most logical since it assumes that churn rate and retention rate is high.

```{r}
best_scenario <- revenue_results[
  which.max(revenue_results$Net_Revenue),
]

print(best_scenario, row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r}
# Average net revenue by assumed churn rate
aggregate(
  Net_Revenue ~ Churn_Rate,
  data = revenue_results,
  FUN = mean
)

# Average net revenue by retention success rate
aggregate(
  Net_Revenue ~ Retention_Success_Rate,
  data = revenue_results,
  FUN = mean
)

# Average net revenue by contact cost
aggregate(
  Net_Revenue ~ Contact_Cost,
  data = revenue_results,
  FUN = mean
)

# Average net revenue by offer cost
aggregate(
  Net_Revenue ~ Offer_Cost,
  data = revenue_results,
  FUN = mean
)
```
